identity.trade: Boats and rope: Coldharbor's slip builds the ferries and flat boats that cross the Silverrun, and its ropewalk is a quarter mile long.

greeting: Keep the pier clear, the nets dry and your questions short.
Strangers in Coldharbor get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: A boat came in with nobody aboard. Fish still in the net. Warm tea in the cup.
Tides follow the moon, they say. Ours follow something else. The old men have stopped betting.
One ferry crosses at night. Nobody has seen its pilot.

opinions.cecily_hawker: Cecily knows the trade. I will say that for Cecily.
opinions.olwen_brine: Olwen is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Coldharbor is boatwrights. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: The fishers come in at dawn and drink till noon. Their wives come at one.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
A seal followed my boat for a mile and spoke. I did not answer.
A boatwright swears the river speaks in the spring melt.

opinions.yorick_fletcher: Yorick undercuts me. I forgive Yorick. Mostly.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
First time in Coldharbor? The Coldharbor Slip is the place to start.
rumour: Hooks, gaffs and anchors. If it holds a boat, I forged it.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
Fish tasted of iron last week. Not bad. Not right.

opinions.kit_overton: Kit has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Kit.
opinions.mellor_applegarth: Mellor undercuts me. I forgive Mellor. Mostly.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Friend! I have a plan. It is a terrible plan. It is going to be wonderful.

greeting: If it is not on the shelf, I can find it. If it cannot be found, I can find you something similar.
Smell that? That is the sea. Or the fish. Hard to say.
rumour: Hooks, floats and twine. If it is thin and sharp, it is a bestseller.
Rope sells out first, then candles, then nails. In that order, every week.
A net came up with a coil of old chain in it, links as long as a forearm. We put it back.
If trade slows, Coldharbor feels it first. If it speeds up, Coldharbor feels it last.

opinions.yorick_fletcher: Yorick undercuts me. I forgive Yorick. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
You will hear Coldharbor before you see it. Ask at the Coldharbor Slip.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
A boat came back empty with its sail torn, as if something had pulled at it.
The ropewalk is a quarter mile long and still too short for the new ferry.

opinions.fulk_brine: Fulk works hard and talks harder.
opinions.sitha_upton: Sitha keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: Pitch is hot, planks are cold, and my temper falls in between.
The Coldharbor Slip is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Black oak for the keel. It never leaks and it never comes back.
The tide marks on the pier are wrong. Higher than last year, higher than the old stone.

opinions.bede_tilley: Bede works hard and talks harder.
opinions.cecily_hawker: Cecily keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Hemp, tar, patience. In that order.
Welcome to Coldharbor. Mind the Coldharbor Slip. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: A coil came back from the water tied in a knot I do not know.
A boy swore he saw a ship at the mouth of the bay with no mast and no crew. The tide took it.

opinions.osric_wicker: Osric works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Lines down by first light, or do not bother.
Tide waits for nobody, and neither does a net.
rumour: Fish came up with eyes gone white. Could be the cold. Could be the water. We threw them back.
The gulls leave the harbour every evening in a line. They did not use to.
A stranger asked at the Coldharbor Slip for the oldest person in Coldharbor. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.bede_tilley: Bede lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.blythe_selby: Blythe knows the trade. I will say that for Blythe.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Hold this. No, higher. There.
If it floats, I have fished from it. If it sank, I have fished it up.
rumour: Rope is dear and getting dearer. Cut a net, you cut a wage.
A light under the water off the point moves against the current.

opinions.blythe_selby: Blythe works hard and talks harder.
opinions.osric_wicker: Osric knows the trade. I will say that for Osric.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: If it floats, I built it. If it sank, somebody else did.
Folk come to Coldharbor for boatwrights. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Someone ordered a boat with a shallow draft and no name. I built it for coin.
The shoals went deep a month early. The old fishers say the cold comes from below.
Ask in Coldharbor who built the Coldharbor Slip and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.bede_tilley: Bede works hard and talks harder.
opinions.osric_wicker: Osric keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: I do not say this often. It is good to see a face I do not need to avoid.

greeting: Salt keeps. People, less so.
Coldharbor is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: The brine pans froze in the night, in autumn. I skimmed ice off the salt in September.
Every few years Coldharbor has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.bede_tilley: Bede knows the trade. I will say that for Bede.
opinions.blythe_selby: Blythe lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
The tide marks on the pier are wrong. Higher than last year, higher than the old stone.

opinions.fulk_brine: Fulk and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A sack by the racks, crusted white, slit and loosely tied.
Wet prints, bare feet, from the water to the sheds and back.
A net cut clean, not torn. The cut edge is still wet.
A glistening trail through flattened reeds, wide as a hand.
Fish bones heaped at the water's edge, unnaturally clean.
A net dragged half out of the water and chewed through.

stashes.say: You carry three coils of tarred rope.
You pick three clean bundles of the healer's herbs.
